north-kaibab-coconino.note: North Kaibab Trail is open to foot traffic through Phantom Ranch, but the National Park Service advises increased caution near Supai Tunnel and the lower trail due to Dragon Bravo Fire burn-scar hazards, including debris flows, rockfalls, and flash flooding with little to no warning even when storms are not visible overhead; hikers should stay alert to posted forecasts and be prepared to move quickly to higher ground. The Flood Watch that was active August 14, 11am to 8pm MST, for this area has expired, and no new flood watch was confirmed active as of the August 15, 2026 morning check; the underlying burn-scar flash flood risk persists through the monsoon season regardless, so check NWS Flagstaff before entering the lower trail. Water is off at the North Kaibab Trailhead and Supai Tunnel, but on at Cottonwood Campground and Manzanita Day Use Area; single bottles and gallon jugs can be purchased at the North Rim General Store from 9am to 4pm daily. Grand Canyon National Park rates today's heat risk at Phantom Ranch as Major. No Extreme Heat Warning was active for the Grand Canyon area below 4000 feet as of the August 15, 2026 morning check. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park (Key Hiking Messages page, last updated August 12, 2026, reconfirmed August 15, 2026); National Weather Service Flagstaff.
